title: Rust DIO admission requires broadcast L2 addr mode; Python never inspects it (over-tightening divergence)
description: Found by security codereview of worker6-dqeg (unicast-dst parity fix). Rust gate authenticated_dio_destination_is_canonical_multicast (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs ~:2145-2172) requires destination_mode() in {None, Elided} for canonical multicast DIO admission. The Python reference admission path (python/src/lichen/rpl/authenticated_dio.py:291-363) never inspects the link frame's address mode — it checks SCHC dispatch, Rule 255, signer-IID source, dst exactly ff02::1a, hop 255 only. Divergence: an Extended-addr (unicast L2) frame carrying a Rule-255 DIO with IPv6 dst exactly ff02::1a and valid signature is ADMITTED by Python but REJECTED by Rust (peer revoked via the uniform admission-failure path). The AddrMode conjunct predates worker6-dqeg (it was in the old multicast branch too). Decide the canonical contract: (a) drop the Rust conjunct for exact Python parity, or (b) keep it as intentional hardening and add addr-mode awareness to Python. If (b), document the interop consequence for senders that unicast-deliver multicast DIOs (e.g. relay re-transmission paths). Related: worker6-dqeg (dst parity, landed), worker6-balm (C-vs-Python admission divergence).
close_reason: Adjudicated option (a): dropped the broadcast-addr-mode conjunct from authenticated_dio_destination_is_canonical_multicast (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs) — gate now requires dst exactly ff02::1a + Rule 255 payload byte, exactly matching the Python reference admission path (authenticated_dio.py), which never inspects link address mode. The addr-mode conjunct was the only over-tightening: C has no addr-mode admission check to diverge (verified by reviewer). New acceptance test authenticated_dio_admission_accepts_unicast_link_frame_with_multicast_dio pins the Extended-addr-to-me + canonical multicast DIO case as admitted; existing unicast-dst rejections unchanged (dst conjunct). Comments updated; reviewer identified the residual END-TO-END divergence (Rust receive_frame lacks Python's NOT_FOR_US destination filter, so Rust admits a superset incl. Extended-to-anyone) — filed as worker6-er31 with the comment pointing there; exploitability negligible per reviewer (signature binds addr-mode bits; all content gates survive). Gates: cargo test -p lichen-schc green under --features std AND std,raw-fragment-codec,test-utils (0 failures); clippy --all-targets no hits in touched files; fmt shows only the 3 pre-existing drift hunks (293/1447/2178, worker-4 preflight scope). Codereview: security pass completed by Kimi K3 (effectively PASS, P3 comment fix + er31 filed); correctness and edge-case passes attempted 2x each via Kimi K3 but timed out mid-run (480-900s) — completed per worker-loop fallback by self-review with targeted verification (callers/error semantics unchanged, test byte-validity incl. RULE_UNCOMPRESSED=255 written by encode_rule255, no stale comments, Elided behavior unchanged, determinism); no defects found.
